status: The migration step (§8 G) of the LTA brief: every existing RAMX, NANDX and BATX source re-read against the Spot / Contract / LTA definitions, with the before/after published in oracle/docs/lta-migration.md (§9.5). A classification is this file's reading of what the source publishes; under the heads design eligibility stays a challenge outcome (OFF_CHANNEL, DUPLICATE_ORIGIN), never a review.

channels.lta: A purchase under a supply agreement of at least one year with committed volume, including prices newly fixed or reset under it.
channels.contract: A negotiated wholesale purchase, supplier → OEM/ODM (BATX: cell maker → vehicle OEM or storage integrator, or a tender award), delivered in the observation period and not under an LTA.
channels.none: Fits none of the above (unterminated quotes, resales without terms, model outputs, test rows): eligible nowhere.
channels.appliedTo: A published assessment is classified by what its publisher says it measures (its own label, methodology and counterparty), since the brief's §6 treats published contract assessments as Contract-channel evidence; a direct price by what the page shows (stock, quantity, terms).

originRule.identity: "amoeba-oracle-origin-v1" + "\n" + publisher + "\n" + report, each trimmed, ASCII-lowercased and with runs of whitespace made one space
originRule.originId: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 identity
originRule.publisher: Whoever first published the price, not a page repeating it: CFM for memorymarket.com and chinaflashmarket.com; TrendForce for trendforce.com, trendforce.cn and EnergyTrend (energytrend.cn); SMM for newenergy.smm.cn, car.smm.cn and metal.com.
originRule.report: The publication series (the table, assessment or price list), never one of its rows: rows of one report share its sample and methodology, so they are one origin (brief §5.1; batx_source_manifest.v1.json: rows of one publisher count once). For CFM the report is its table's own slug (rdimmcontract, ddroem, ddrchannel, ssdoem, ssdchannel, emmc, ufs, nandflash, ddr).
originRule.sameAs: The rule of channel_molds.v1.json (originRule), so originIds here are the ones heads will declare.
originRule.duplicates: Within one board (mainnet, dev, or the catalog), item and channel, the first row of an origin carries it and every later one names it in duplicateOf: on-chain sources first in source-id order (the inventory order routing uses), then off-chain candidates by creation, then catalog rows in manifest order. collapse is 'republication' (the same row again, on another site or listing) or 'sibling-row' (another row of the same report). Under heads the first live source of an origin carries it.

boards.mainnet: Mainnet oracle as served by https://api.amoeba.farm/v1/oracle/public-snapshot and /oracle/source-candidates/recent, read 2026-10-29 ~05:30 UTC: RAMX/NANDX Oct 26 (launch, Game) and BATX Nov 26 (source window). RAMX/NANDX Nov 26 are not open on mainnet.
boards.dev: Dev chain as served by the dev API (127.0.0.1:4500), read 2026-10-29 ~05:30 UTC: the launch months (same 35 sources as mainnet), RAMX/NANDX/BATX Nov 26 and Dec 26 (one source per bucket, dev-oracle-chip-sources.json) and the off-chain candidate store; the Jan 27 months have no sources yet.
boards.catalog: governance/batx_source_manifest.v1.json: candidate series documented for BATX, not on any chain.
boards.notIncluded: governance/commodity_submission_spec.v*.json 'sources' (Micron, KIOXIA, TrendForce DRAM/NAND tables, DRAMeXchange FAQ) are references for product definitions, not sources; the SKU manifests list part numbers, not sources; futures/ops test URLs are fixtures. The chain experiment mirrors mainnet months and was not read separately.

blockerCodes.terms_ban: TrendForce Terms of Use §5(h) prohibit using its prices in connection with a prediction market (batx_source_manifest.v1.json).
blockerCodes.licence_required: The publisher limits commercial use or redistribution without a written licence (CFM's copyright notice; InfoLink, SMM, Mysteel, Fastmarkets, Benchmark terms).
